name: Zambian Sign Language
sweep_summary: Zambian Sign Language is not in the catalog and this search of works with stress in the title turned up a single stress-keyword title, Hicks Jr. 1979 (Glottolog ref 520280), which is about the acoustic effects of psychological 'situational stress' on spoken speech; Glottolog itself says the link to zsl was assigned computationally from the keyword 'situational'. It is not about word stress, not about Zambia, and not about a signed language; the chapter is paywalled at Benjamins (DOI 10.1075/cilt.9.32hic), but a Google Books snippet of its opening lines and the Crossref record settle its content. No first-hand statement on stress/prosody of Zambian Sign Language exists in anything reached (our earlier reading in the same directory read Chanda 1997 and Chibwe 2015, neither of which mentions stress). the item judgement rests on the DOI/Crossref/Glottolog/Google Books records opened.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page for zamb1239 (classification note citing Chanda 1997: 194-195; Ethnologue 2025 for status).
sources.note: No descriptive references; the six 'glottolog_refs' attached to this key in Garrod & Terras 2000; Hlavac et al. 2020; Ameka 2003; Ruiz de Mendoza & Lozano-Palacio 2021; Belaj & Tanackovic 2022; Holm et al. 2003) are keyword noise ('situational', 'verbal') and do not concern Zambian Sign Language at all.

sources.citation: Chibwe, Juliet. 2015. Contribution of sign language variations to academic performance of learners with hearing impairments in selected Copperbelt and Lusaka primary special schools in Zambia. Dissertation (MEd), University of Zambia.https://dspace.unza.zm/handle/123456789/4261
sources.note: Nothing about ZSL stress/prosody. Sections 2.5.3-2.5.4.3 (pp. 23-26) are a literature review of ASL / Kenyan SL phonological variation (Lucas et al., Akach & Okombo 1997, hold-movement model), not a description of Zambian SL; the only ZSL-specific linguistic content is lexical variation anecdotes (e.g. BEER by province) attributed to Mbewe 2009.

sources.citation: Chanda, Vincent M. 1997. Lexicography and sign language engineering: The Zambian experience. Lexikos 7 (AFRILEX-reeks/series 7): 192-206. DOI 10.5788/7-1-980.
sources.note: Nothing. p.194 gives only the generic four-parameter sign structure ('Minimally an SL sign consists of four components.. hand shape.. location.. movement.. orientation'); the rest is ZSL history (Magwero school 1955, ASL influence) and the ZNAD dictionary's design. a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing.
Nothing; no linguistic description, dictionary or grammar cited.
